entries.topic: Yarvin's own later accounts (NYT The Interview, Jan 2025)

claims.text: Yarvin: Washington, Lincoln and FDR were 'basically national CEOs'; 'it's not even that democracy is bad, it's just that it's very weak'; FDR said 'give me absolute power or I'll take it anyway'

On RAGE, Yarvin said to 'treat it like a company that goes out of business, but sort of more so', and argued former officials should be treated as ordinary people who served a bad regime; a new regime 'can't be' about bayoneting professors; 'Winning means these are your people now'
On Breivik and Mandela: 'I prefer to condemn them both'; both 'basically killed innocent people'
Marchese quoted Yarvin's line 'It is very difficult to argue that the Civil War made anyone's life more pleasant, including that of freed slaves'; Yarvin said abolition 'was a necessary step'
Yarvin said it is 'not exactly time for that yet', that he is 'an outsider' whose ideas reach power mainly through staffers and younger people online
Marchese quoted Yarvin's line on white nationalism: 'It is strategically barren'

Yarvin: monarchies 'don't generally see a Holocaust'; Fortune 500 CEOs 'wouldn't be Hitler or Stalin'; one must 'just hope somehow that this is the right individual'; a monarch 'should operate like a startup CEO'

Yarvin said the administration was 'barely scratching the surface' of needed change and that his influence is 'more through the kids in the administration'; a Vance adviser said the two had met 'like once'
CNN reported Thiel told The Atlantic (2023) he did not think Yarvin's ideas would 'work' but found him an 'interesting and powerful' historian
CNN reported Yarvin's 2022 'ninjas' idea to 'seize all points of power, without respect for paper protections'
Danielle Allen at the Harvard Faculty Club debate: 'it is not the case that autocracies over the course of history have delivered good for human beings'

sources.label: Transcript of 'The Interview: Curtis Yarvin Says Democracy Is Done. Powerful Conservatives Are Listening', David Marchese, New York Times, 18 January 2025 (podcast transcript)
CNN, 'Curtis Yarvin wants to replace American democracy with a form of monarchy led by a CEO', 30 May 2025

entries.topic: Yarvin's program in his own words (UR posts as quoted with citations)

claims.text: 'A formalist manifesto' (UR, 23 April 2007): 'We need a rule that tells us whose wallet is whose'; 'Formalism says: let's figure out exactly who has what, now, and give them a little fancy certificate'
'Good government as good customer service' (25 May 2007): 'Fnargland is a business. Like any business, it has no reason at all to alienate its customers'
'Why I am not a white nationalist' (22 Nov 2007): 'I am not a white nationalist because I don't find white nationalism useful or effective'

'Patchwork: A Positive Vision (Part 1)' (13 Nov 2008), on a sovereign corporation's surplus residents: 'Sell their slums out from under them, obviously;' 'demo everything, spray for roaches, rodents, and pit bulls,' 'possibly a little aerial bombing;' 'erect new residential districts suitable for Russian oligarchs'; these people, 'bezonians', can emigrate to any other realm

'Gentle Introduction to UR (Part 9b)' (Oct 2009): 'All the Reaction must do is convince reasonable, educated men and women of good will'; Part 9d: 'the Party holds power for only as long as it takes to hire a qualified administrator'

In a 2012 talk to California tech workers Moldbug said 'If Americans want to change their government, they're going to have to get over their dictator phobia', called for 'a national CEO [or] what's called a dictator', 'There's really no other solution'; suggested a Red-State and a Blue-State dictator; item one of Justine Tunney's White House petition (retire all government employees) came verbatim from the talk
Pein 2014: Yarvin held the title 'benevolent dictator for life' at Tlon; Thiel invested in Tlon
Yarvin: 'The cathedral is essentially the reification of the legitimate sources of information'
Princeton holds 'Moldbug on Carlyle' (2010), a lightly edited 82-page compilation of three UR essays on Carlyle from 2009-10, in copyright

Kofman: Patchwork (2008) proposed splitting nations into small sovereign statelets like Singapore or Dubai run by corporate 'sovcorps' under a secret board; the 'humane alternative to genocide' post proposed confining marginal urban populations in virtual reality

entries.topic: The hard posts: wording, dates and sources

claims.text: 2008 post ('Patchwork 2', Nov 2008) on residents not productive: 'convert them into biodiesel, which can help power the Muni buses', then 'just kidding'; goal: 'a humane alternative to genocide'; 'virtualize' them in 'permanent solitary confinement' connected to an 'immersive virtual-reality interface'
2012 BIL speech: 'If Americans want to change their government, they're going to have to get over their dictator phobia'; RAGE = 'Retire All Government Employees'

'Why Carlyle Matters' (UR, July 2009): 'Not all humans are born the same...' some 'more suited to mastery than slavery'; 'A person makes a good slave if he is loyal, patient, and not exceptionally bright or stubborn'; 'most parsimoniously explained by genetic differences' (blockquoted as his own writing; surrounding text not shown)

'Right-wing terrorism as folk activism' (UR, 23 July 2011): 'At least he shot communists, not Muslims. He gored the matador and not the cape'; 'ABB is a terrorist. Nelson Mandela is a terrorist'; a vulgar line addressed to those who condemn Breivik but adore Mandela
Yarvin appeared on Fox Nation's Tucker Carlson Today on 8 September 2021

Land quotes Moldbug: 'It should be obvious that, although I am not a white nationalist, I am not exactly allergic to the stuff', calling it 'the most marginalized and socially excluded belief system in the history of the world' (e-book p. 26); Land credits Moldbug with neocameralism ('a state is a business which owns a country'), the Cathedral, and names him 'supreme Sith Lord of the neoreactionaries' (pp. 5-6)

Moldbug, quoted by Land: although the full neocameralist approach 'has never been tried', its closest equivalents are Frederick the Great's enlightened absolutism and 'Hong Kong, Singapore and Dubai' (p. 6)
